found: Here secondly is the section where we establish our own position. Now suppose three different types of beings--a pleasure being, a human, and a craving spirit, each with their own karma--sit down together and look upon a glass filled with water, the thing we define as "wet and flowing." The glass of water is not at this point one thing which is simultaneously three different objects. Neither is it necessary in this situation for there to be three identical valid perceptions. And when the glass full of wet and flowing water occurs, it occurs with three different, distinct parts to it.
